Chapter 7: Navigating Common Challenges and Missteps
Even when you start out with the best intentions, you’re bound to hit a few bumps as you try putting these leadership practices into action. Let’s be honest, old habits, time crunches, and the overall vibe of your company can all make things tricky. But here’s the thing—just recognizing these challenges, and knowing how to deal with them, makes it much easier to keep moving forward.
One of the biggest hurdles? Inconsistency. Maybe you praise someone’s effort one day, but forget the next. Or you let a little problem go, and before you know it, it’s grown into something bigger. Sound familiar? The trick is to make feedback a regular part of your routine, not something you squeeze in when you remember. Setting reminders, like we mentioned earlier, can really help. And don’t be afraid to lean on your team or your peers—hold each other accountable, and you’ll all get better at it.
Another challenge a lot of people face is feeling awkward about giving corrective feedback. Nobody wants to hurt someone’s feelings or risk damaging a relationship. But here’s what helps: focus on the behavior, not the person, and always lead with empathy. The point isn’t to assign blame—it’s to help each other grow. And as your team sees that feedback is fair and consistent, the nerves fade, and trust starts to build.
Sometimes, you’ll run into resistance from team members who are used to a totally different management style. Maybe they think your new approach is just a trend, or they’re uncomfortable with being more transparent and accountable. That’s when patience and persistence really matter. Keep modeling the behaviors you want to see, and explain the “why” behind your decisions. Over time, you’ll find people start to come around.
Here are a few practical ways to help overcome resistance:
Get your team involved in setting goals and figuring out what success looks like. Share stories about how these practices have made a difference for others. And don’t pretend change is easy—acknowledge it’s tough, and invite your team to share their thoughts on how you can all make the process better.
And finally, remember—mistakes are part of the journey. Nobody gets it right every time. If you miss a goal or a piece of feedback doesn’t land well, treat it as a chance to learn. Reflect on what happened, make a few tweaks, and keep going. Being open to learning like this? It sends a powerful message to your whole team.
